input.note: Full game executable; production strings/imports retained, internal/debug labels stripped. All eight changed constants and derived requested outcomes checked by executable oracles using the actual mutated game source/objects. Weapon oracle substitutes random/world I/O boundaries; no WAD/gameplay test.

community.source: Reused unchanged source, built extension and installed dependencies preserved from earlier audit; no new community dependencies installed.

correctness: Exact integer field match to the frozen private key. Missing, duplicate and unknown fields fail. Report complete question and full-session pass separately. Evidence checked separately; no LLM judge.
isolation: Fresh ephemeral Codex process and empty workspace per run. Shell, browser, account apps, memory, plugins, other agents and host skill discovery disabled. MCP is the only permitted analysis surface. No tool can read the source, oracle or symbols. REA receives the normally installed bundled skill and full stock catalog with static-selected-target scope guard.
timing: Serial sessions. All backends are fully analyzed before agent timing. Ours and community use copies of the same canonical Ghidra project. REA stock open_binary plus list_procedures forces its own analysis of identical stripped bytes. Record setup separately; agent time includes Codex startup, reasoning, tools and final answer. Normal OS and provider prompt caches remain enabled.
tokens: Raw input, cached subset and output from turn.completed. Reasoning is included in output. Subscription invoice unavailable; any USD figures are labelled API-equivalent estimates. Unknown usage is never zero.
limits: One privately mutated source-built ARM64 Doom executable; no packers, C++, GUI app, Windows or general-native superiority claim.
Tiny gunshot question also appears in the six-question real round; five questions are new. Do not tune implementation or questions to model answers between rounds.
Static analysis only. No WAD/gameplay benchmark.
The current npm release differs from the earlier REA 6.5.0 source audit; old bugs must not be presented as current-version failures.

amendment.reason: Post-run audit found that macOS rejects RLIMIT_AS in the shared calculator subprocess. All six attempted calculator calls in the first real round failed (ours three; community three; REA did not use the calculator). All answers were correct, but efficiency was affected by the broken shared control.
amendment.fix: Keep the two-second CPU limit and four-second parent timeout on Darwin; use RLIMIT_AS only on supported non-Darwin platforms. A new real-subprocess test verifies the complete calculator route. No memory-cap guarantee is made on Darwin.
